title: AEO Recognition and Application Procedure
summary: The concept of 'applicants' for Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) status has evolved from a basic application submission process into a highly structured, multi-stage institutional framework. Over time, the process has shifted from simple document submission to a rigorous system involving specialized AEO Centers, evaluation teams, intelligence reporting, and formal rejection/deficiency notification protocols.

evolution.procedure: Transitioned from manual application to a standardized, time-bound, and committee-driven evaluation process.
evolution.institutions: Shifted from general NBR oversight to the creation of a dedicated AEO Center and specialized evaluation teams.
evolution.transparency: Increased formalization of communication through standardized forms for deficiencies, rejections, and temporary certifications.

timeline.change: Established initial eligibility criteria for AEO applicants including compliance records and financial standing.
Formalized the AEO Center's role in processing, evaluating, and notifying applicants of deficiencies or rejections.
Introduced granular operational procedures, including intelligence reporting, specific timelines for deficiency correction, and inter-departmental coordination.
Refined the committee structure and formal certification issuance (temporary vs. permanent) processes.

Authorized Economic Operator: This clause outlines the mandatory eligibility criteria for applicants seeking status as an Authorized Economic Operator.
Applicants must demonstrate a sustained period of business operation in Bangladesh, a clean compliance record with customs and tax laws, and a period of being free from proven offences.

Financial eligibility requirements include meeting specific thresholds for authorized capital, paid-up capital, or annual turnover, alongside requirements for average annual import or export volume based on the applicant's business category.

Applicants must maintain a satisfactory payment history for revenue duties and ensure that any penalties incurred in customs or tax matters within a specific prior period do not exceed a set percentage of the value of goods or services.

(৪) আবেদন প্রাপ্তির ১৫ (পনেরো) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে সেন্টার হইতে নিযুক্ত মূল্যায়নকারী টিম প্রতিটি আবেদন, দাখিলকৃত Self-Assessment Questionnaire (SAQ) ও উহার সহিত দাখিলকৃত দলিলাদি যাচাই-বাছাই করিবে এবং যাচাই-বাছাইকালে অতিরিক্ত কোনো তথ্য বা দলিলাদির প্রয়োজন হইলে পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনেরো) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে উহা দাখিলের জন্য আবেদনকারীকে লিখিতভাবে অনুরোধ করিবে:

(১৭) মহাপরিচালক, সেন্টার এর নিকট হইতে প্রাপ্ত সুপারিশ পর্যালোচনাস্তে কমিটি গোয়েন্দা তথ্য ও ঝুঁকি বিবেচনাপূর্বক অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটরের স্বীকৃতি প্রদান অথবা আবেদন প্রত্যাখ্যান অথবা শর্ত সাপেক্ষে বা সাময়িক স্বীকৃতি প্রদান, অথবা প্রতিষ্ঠানকে পূর্ণাঙ্গ তথ্য-উপাত্তসহ বা প্রয়োজনীয় কার্যাবলি গ্রহণপূর্বক পুনরায় আবেদন করিবার সিদ্ধান্ত ৩০ (ত্রিশ) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে প্রদান করিয়া সেন্টারকে অবহিত করিবে:

Applicants may receive a temporary certificate subject to specific conditions which must be fulfilled within a set timeframe, with provisions for a limited extension if necessary.
Failure to meet the stipulated conditions for a temporary certificate within the permitted time can lead to a recommendation for the cancellation of such certificate.

Decisions regarding the issuance or cancellation of certificates can be challenged by the applicant or the Center through a formal request for reconsideration submitted to the Chairman of the National Board of Revenue.
National Board of Revenue: The Chairman of the National Board of Revenue is the designated authority to hear and decide upon appeals for the reconsideration of decisions made by the Authorized Economic Operator committee regarding certificate issuance or cancellation.
Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Commi: This committee is responsible for deciding on the grant of Authorized Economic Operator status, the issuance of temporary certificates, and the review of recommendations for the cancellation of such certificates.
The committee holds the power to finalize the cancellation of temporary certificates based on recommendations received from the Director General.
Director General of the Center: The Director General is responsible for issuing official certificates or temporary certificates in the prescribed forms and notifying applicants of any rejected applications within a specified working day period.
The Director General monitors the compliance of institutions holding temporary certificates and may grant an extension for fulfilling conditions under unavoidable circumstances.
If temporary certificate conditions remain unmet, the Director General is authorized to recommend the cancellation of the certificate to the Authorized Economic Operator committee.
